chunks: And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:
The fasting person has two joys: a joy when he breaks his fast, and a joy when he meets his Lord, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.إِفْطَارِهِ: his breaking of the fast; the time when the fast ends
key_terms.رَبِّهِ: his Lord; Allah as the one to whom the servant returns
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic; an honorific expression glorifying Allah
key_terms.فَرْحَتَانِ: two joys; two distinct occasions of happiness and delight
key_terms.لِقَاءِ: meeting; the encounter in the Hereafter
key_terms.لِلصَّائِمِ: for the fasting person; referring to the one observing sawm (fasting)

ai.seo_question: What are the two joys of the fasting person in this hadith of Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq عليه السلام teaches that fasting brings both an immediate joy and an ultimate joy. One is experienced at iftar, and the other is reserved for the meeting with Allah, highlighting the spiritual and eschatological reward of sawm (fasting).

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1780 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"The fasting person has two joys: a joy when he breaks his fast and a joy when he meets his Lord (azj), the Almighty."
